extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and newspaper reporters (esp. those writing society and sports pages)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples for composing society (social and personal) news items for newspapers — how to style society columns, what to include or avoid, and when certain social items may be treated as regular news. The page also contains illustrative sports reports showing conventions of sports writing (narrative, quotes, box scores, technical detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a society department under a society editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest in social and personal news is so great that practically every newspaper maintains a society department under the direction of a society editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize coverage: assign a dedicated department and editor responsible for social/personal news to ensure consistent coverage and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and style determined by social usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and style suitable to such news are partly determined by social usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt tone, phrasing, and emphasis to prevailing social conventions and expectations of the readership when composing society items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style may differ in society columns
rubrics_metrics.description: The typographical style of the society columns often differs somewhat from that of other parts of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that layout, type treatment, and column conventions for society pages can and often should depart from general news pages to suit social-news norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give variety; avoid stock phrases and trite description
rubrics_metrics.description: Society news taxes the writer’s ability to give variety to stories of the same kind of events as they take place day by day. In no other kind of news is he more frequently tempted to use stock phrases over and over again. It is possible, however, to give considerable variety to society stories as well as to avoid trite, colorless, description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consciously avoid clichés and repeated stock phrasing; vary approach and descriptive detail so recurring event types (weddings, engagements, parties) remain fresh and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat unusual social events as regular news when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual courtships, engagements, and weddings may be treated as regular news; in that case the stories of them are not often placed in the society section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a social item has news value beyond routine society interest (novelty, public significance), consider writing it as straight news and placing it outside the society column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop humorous or pathetic possibilities without violating good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Such news not infrequently has humorous and pathetic possibilities that the writer may develop without violating the canons of good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit human-interest angles (humor, pathos) to enliven social stories, but balance color with respect and adherence to standards of taste and decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, dramatic narrative in sports reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated by passages like the Cobb play: dramatic lead-ins and colorful metaphors (e.g., ‘Cobb pulled the wool over their eyes like a ‘‘sharper’’’) enliven the account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a striking moment or image, use lively verbs and metaphor to dramatize action while preserving factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include direct quotations and sideline chatter where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Coach lines and dialogue (example: quotes attributed to Hughie Jennings) provide color and character to the account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intersperse pertinent direct quotes (coaches, players) and audible sideline remarks to give immediacy and voice to the report, ensuring accuracy in attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide play-by-play sequencing and decisive moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Game accounts recount the sequence of plays (steals, singles, runs) and describe how scoring developed (e.g., Cobb’s steal and subsequent runs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present events in clear chronological order, highlighting turning points and decisive plays so readers can follow how the outcome was reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include complete factual/statistical details (box score elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Game coverage supplies a box score and detailed statistics: hits, errors, stolen bases, earned runs, sacrifice hits, left on bases, first base on error, bases on balls, hits off pitchers, hit by pitcher, strikeouts, time of game, umpires, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alongside narrative, provide the official statistics and box score elements so readers have the factual record; include names, figures, and relevant game metadata (time, umpires).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide technical analysis and context (times, records, technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crew and regatta reports discuss times, upstream/downstream effects on times, stroke rate, rigging and technique, coaching influence, and comparisons with records (e.g., Yale/Harvard times and stroke observations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain technical factors that affected performance (conditions, stroke rate, rigging), report official times/splits, compare with records, and attribute coaching or tactical causes where justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report playing conditions and their effect on play
rubrics_metrics.description: Match accounts note conditions (e.g., courts sogged by rains; wind affecting golf holes) and connect them to player performance and outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe weather/field/court conditions and explain how they influenced tactics and results to give readers fuller understanding of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrate key sequences and turning points in match play
rubrics_metrics.description: Tennis and golf accounts focus on pivotal games/holes, scoring runs, and mental/technical shifts (e.g., momentum swings, missed putts) that decided the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and narrate the critical moments and shifts in momentum, summarizing how they changed the contest and contributed to the final result.
